title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
claim: A two-stage procedure first trains specialized components on semantic data partitions, then reuses them as frozen initialization while only a router is learned.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers separating Stage 1 and Stage 2
description: A wide three-panel pipeline diagram split by dashed vertical lines into Stage 1 (left and middle) and Stage 2 (right). The left panel, 'Semantic Clustering', shows a rounded box of original data as colored markers (green diamonds, blue stars, purple circles, orange squares, red squares). Arrows lead to colored ellipses C1 to CN, which are then split into sub-clusters S1 and S2 at Level 2. The middle panel, 'Training MLP Layer', shows image and text encoder stacks of Fused Dense and Dense layers, a Constrained Sampler, a Contrastive Loss box, and extracted MLP weights in a pink box. The right panel, 'Training MoE Model', has the same encoders with Fused MoE layers, a Normal Sampler, and weights initialized from Stage 1. Blue and orange pastel backgrounds distinguish the image and text encoders.
caption: Illustration of our main training pipeline. Stage 1 performs semantic clustering to group original data into distinct clusters ($C_0$, $C_1$, $C_2$, ..., \(C_N\)) (left). Data from each cluster trains a corresponding MLP layer, with all MLPs training concurrently (middle). In Stage 2, the trained MLP weights from Stage 1 serve as initialization for the MoE experts. During this stage, only the router network is trained while the expert weights remain frozen (right).
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a promising approach for scaling deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. However, existing MoE adaptations for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models suffer from significant computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of zero-shot capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose CLIP-FMoE, a novel approach that integrates MoE architecture into CLIP fine-tuning. Our method uses Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning, a pipeline that trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization. Additionally, we introduce a Fusion Gate mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves consistent improvements on downstream tasks while preserving zero-shot capabilities. Furthermore, our method demonstrates robust performance across varying context lengths, making it particularly suitable for diverse real-world applications.
